title: Enhancing the Role of the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP) to Tackle Workplace and Job Discrimination
what_it_is: Enhancing the Role of the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP) to Tackle Workplace and Job Discrimination

sections.label: Older worker employment and unemployment
sections.summary: Employment rate for workers aged 55 to 64 rose from 57.2% in 2008 to 66.8% in 2018, while unemployment rates for older age groups showed mixed recent changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For workers aged 55 to 64, the employment rate rose from 57.2% in 2008 to 66.8% in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Our annual average resident unemployment rate by age does show that unemployment rates for those aged 40-49 and 50 over, have fallen slightly in 2018 from 2017, but more recent quarterly seasonally adjusted unemployment rate for 50 and over has risen slightly.

sections.label: Employment laws against discriminatory dismissal
sections.summary: Singapore's employment laws largely protect employees against wrongful dismissal on discriminatory grounds such as age, pregnancy or family responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Singapore's employment laws largely protect employees against wrongful dismissal on discriminatory grounds, such as age, pregnancy or family responsibilities.

sections.label: UK older workforce challenge
sections.summary: In the United Kingdom, employers are challenged to increase their older workforce by 12% by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: My first suggestion: in the United Kingdom (UK), employers are challenged to increase their older workforce by 12% by 2020.

sections.label: Certification for age-inclusive companies
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether certification could be introduced for companies that meet specific requirements to provide age-inclusive and diverse work environments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Having the intention is admirable and improving the workplace is always an ongoing process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: But can we go one step further and introduce certification for companies that meet specific requirements to provide age-inclusive and diverse work environments?

sections.label: MOM assessment of Singaporean Core
sections.summary: MOM would assess companies' Singaporean Core against their industry, their commitment to developing it and their value to the country, with weak companies advised to build it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: To address these concerns, the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) would assess whether companies have a Singaporean Core compared with the rest of their industry and look at their commitment to developing this Core as well as the value of the company to the country.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Companies that are weak in all three criteria will be advised to build their Singaporean Core.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: But if they remain resistant, they will face closer scrutiny and could see their Employment Pass privileges curtailed.

sections.label: Localisation targets for companies
sections.summary: The speaker suggests companies set localisation targets for their workforce in consultation with tripartite partners, to support Singapore's competitiveness and workforce sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: There must be greater efforts at localisation over a period of time, which is needed to support Singapore's competitiveness, workforce sustainability and building our Singapore Core.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I would suggest that companies set localisation targets for their workforce, in consultation with the tripartite partners.

sections.label: Capability Transfer Programme for firms
sections.summary: The Capability Transfer Programme supports firms bringing in foreign specialists to transfer capabilities to the local workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: One carrot approach is via the Capability Transfer Programme (CTP), as we all know, which currently supports firms to bring in foreign specialists to transfer capabilities to the local workforce.

sections.label: Expanding CTP and EP criteria
sections.summary: The speaker suggests expanding the CTP to transfer capabilities from foreign employees already in Singapore to local workers, and regularly updating Employment Pass criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: My suggestion is, can we consider expanding the CTP to support transfer of capabilities from foreign employees currently "already employed" in Singapore to local workers, with the eventual aim of localising jobs, working in tandem with the localisation targets I had mentioned earlier?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: My third suggestion: Mr Deputy Speaker, I also feel that the Employment Pass eligibility criteria ought to be regularly updated and tightened when needed, appropriately.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For example, the current minimum salary of $3,600 for young graduates could be too low.

sections.label: Older worker employment rates
sections.summary: Employment rates for older workers have been trending upwards better than many developed countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The employment rates for our older workers have been trending upwards better than many developed countries.

sections.label: Naming errant companies publicly
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Ministry would consider publicly naming companies where TAFEP and MOM have clear evidence of errant practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: For the egregious cases where TAFEP and MOM have clear evidence of errant practices, would the Ministry consider publicly naming these companies?

sections.label: Special Employment Credit signal
sections.summary: The Special Employment Credit signals that hiring older workers has value beyond what companies perceive at face value.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The Special Employment Credit is an important economic and policy signal that there is value to hiring older workers beyond what is perceived at face value by companies.

sections.label: Green lanes and inclusive workforce
sections.summary: The speaker suggests granting exemplary companies administrative green lanes and longer leases, and says an inclusive workforce can be a competitive workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Perhaps, the Ministry can also consider granting exemplary companies with administrative green lanes and longer leases perhaps to show the Government's commitment to building an inclusive workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: An inclusive workforce can, in fact, be a competitive workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Yet, many athletes are playing well into their late 30s and 40s now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Some of them are hired specifically for their experience and locker room influence for the younger players.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The Chinese have a saying, "上有政策，下有对策“。It roughly translates to, "For every policy, there is a counter move." Therefore, the way ahead is not one necessarily of more legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: It is one whereby we affirm that every worker matters through trust and true belief amongst workers, employers and the Government.

sections.label: MOM enforcement against errant employers
sections.summary: Over three years, MOM took enforcement action against about 900 errant employers for such infringements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Over the last three years, MOM has taken enforcement action against about 900 errant employers for such infringements.

sections.label: Watchlist firms and EP outcomes
sections.summary: Since 2016, about 600 firms were watchlisted, 2,300 EP applications rejected or withdrawn, and over 3,800 Singaporean PMETs hired.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Since 2016, we have placed about 600 firms across all sectors on the watchlist.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: A total of 2,300 EP applications have been rejected by MOM or withdrawn by employers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: In addition, employers on the FCF watchlist have hired more than 3,800 Singaporean PMETs to date.

sections.label: EP salary criterion review
sections.summary: MOM regularly reviews the EP salary criterion using local PMET salaries, with a $3,600 minimum for young graduates with good qualifications.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: MOM regularly reviews the EP salary criterion, taking reference from local PMET salaries and a similar experience in seniority.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: This is to ensure that local PMETs are not disadvantaged based on cost as their salaries go up over time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: To clarify, the minimum salary requirement of $3,600 applies to young graduates with good qualifications.

sections.label: Older Singaporeans employed today
sections.summary: 500,000 older Singaporeans are employed today, compared to about 270,000 ten years ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: More older Singaporeans are employed today than ever before, or 500,000 today, compared to about half, 270,000 just 10 years ago.

sections.label: Singapore ranked on hiring foreign labour
sections.summary: In a recent World Economic Forum ranking, Singapore was ranked 93rd for ease of hiring foreign labour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: For example, in a recent global competitiveness ranking by the World Economic Forum, Singapore was ranked 93rd in terms of ease of hiring foreign labour.

sections.label: CTP support for companies
sections.summary: MOM introduced the CTP, and since its 2017 start over 120 companies and 800 local workers are expected to benefit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: In fact, MOM introduced the CTP to support companies to transfer global expertise and capabilities to Singaporean workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: And since the start of the CTP in 2017, more than 120 companies and 800 local workers are expected to benefit from CTP-supported projects.
